messages:
tomas: Quick thread — proposal: move attribution/join out of the ingest fast path into a dedicated attribution service that subscribes to the ingest stream and emits billing events. tradeoffs below, want quick take.

alice: high level: why separate?

tomas: primary reasons: 1) reduce tail latency on customer-facing ingest, 2) make attribution logic independently deployable and auditable, 3) allow multiple attribution strategies (coarse, strict) without touching ingest.

raj: sounds reasonable. concerns: increased eventual consistency, more late-arrival cases, and more moving parts to reconcile for invoices.

emily: agree with raj. also curious about costs — duplicating storage/compute for another consumer could be non-trivial.

platform-bot: note: moving heavy joins off ingest may reduce p95 by ~30-50% in similar projects.

tomas: cost note: we can optimize by making attribution service able to do tiered modes — realtime best-effort + background strict pass for audits. so customer-facing events get a preliminary attribution quickly, then an authoritative billing event later.

alice: how would clients observe the difference? we need clear contract.

tomas: plan: augment event schema with attribution_state + attribution_version and keep initial attribution optional. example: ```{ "attribution_state": "provisional|final", "attribution_version": "v2" }```

emily: nice. that gives us clear semantics. will break older consumers though?

raj: we should default to adding fields non-breaking. consumers can ignore unknown fields. but for internal downstreams (billing job) we need a strict contract: only consume final events for invoicing.

audit-bot: created audit ticket AF-422: "attribution authoritative-pass verification"

tomas: reconciliation story: attribution svc writes its outputs to an append-only billing topic + writes a compacted reference table (by request_id) for quick lookups. reconciler will compare ingest-derived provenance vs billing topic.

alice: how do we handle late-arrivals / retroactive corrections? e.g., model routing changed, attribution needs to be re-run for a batch from 10m ago.

tomas: we support reprocessing range windows. attribution svc retains a reprocess API: give time range or request_ids, it will recompute + emit correction events with correction=True and new sequence numbers. billing consumers must be idempotent by (request_id, seq).

raj: idempotency is key. we should require billing events include a stable ledger_key and seq. also include prev_hash to form a linked chain for easy diffing.

emily: cryptographic chaining sounds heavy but useful for audits. proposal: each billing event includes event_hash and prior_event_hash for that request_id partition; reconciler can detect missing/corrupt sequences quickly.

alice: what about cross-region routing? attribution svc might be regional for latency, but billing needs global view.

tomas: model: regional attribution -> publish region-tagged billing events to a global hub that merges and dedupes by ledger_key. Must ensure stable shard keys (tenant_id + request_id fingerprint) so global merge is deterministic.

raj: merge/dedupe logic can live in a single global aggregator (stateless stream job) that writes final to authoritative ledger. aggregator must be idempotent and handle out-of-order. use monotonic seq + watermarking.

emily: watermarks are tricky given spikes and retries. we should keep a long enough grace period and expose a "finalized_at" timestamp. invoices only lock after finalized_at + SLA window.

alice: audit requirements: customers want proof of charges. we should expose an audit view that includes original ingest payload (fingerprint), attribution decisions, and reconciler justification. PII redaction applied.

tomas: agreed. implementation: store provenance envelope alongside billing events in cold storage for configured retention (default 90d). add ability to attach a signed manifest (hashes) to an invoice export.

raj: what about sampling to control costs? e.g., high-volume tenants — maybe run provisional attribution for all, final attribution only for sampled or on-demand.

emily: sampling + on-demand reprocess seems fine for metrics and fraud detection, but customers paying per-token will demand exact accounting for invoices. sampling can't be used for chargeable events unless customer opts in.

alice: ops concerns: runbook for attribution svc failure modes? what happens if the subscription lags or a partition dies?

tomas: plan: attribution svc is consumer group with checkpointing; if lag grows > X minutes we switch ingress to fallback attribution mode (best-effort inline) for affected tenants to maintain functionality. create alerting and auto-catchup jobs.

platform-bot: suggested alert thresholds: WARNING at 5m lag, CRITICAL at 30m lag.

raj: fallback inline attribution might be approximated; we need to label events with fallback_reason and ensure reconciler can surface differences to billing team.

emily: also ensure schema versioning strategy: use semantic versioning for attribution rulesets. events should include attribution_ruleset_id so we can backtrace charged amounts to a ruleset revision.

alice: rollout plan?

tomas: phased: 1) attr svc alpha on low-volume tenant subset, emit only provisional events. 2) enable final-run for selected tenants + run reconciler in read-only mode to detect diffs. 3) add correction path + idempotency enforcement. 4) promote to default and deprecate inline joins.

raj: add a canary where billing anchor (small charge) is verified end-to-end before full invoice.

emily: one more: developer ergonomics — provide a local-mode dockerized attribution that can run on a developer laptop for rule testing and offline audits.

tomas: good idea. will add to RFC follow-up.

alice: ok, next steps from eng-platform side?

tomas: I'll draft an RFC with: schema changes, service contract, reprocess API, ledger format, reconciler contract, rollback semantics, runbooks, and cost estimate. want reviewers: @alice, @raj, @emily.

alice: thumbs up. add expected telemetry: counts of provisional vs final, avg reconciliation diffs, cost per 1M events.

platform-bot: RFC draft created: rfc/attr-service-draft-3123456789.md

emily: putting AF-422 on my board to start audit harness work.

audit-bot: AF-422 assigned to emily.

raj: will sketch reconciler POC this week.

alice: thanks — let's keep the convo in the RFC thread after draft. :thumbsup:
